title: APIC (Advanced Programmable Interrupt Controller)
summary: The APIC (Local APIC + I/O APIC) is the modern interrupt controller for x86 multi-core systems. Local APIC: per-CPU, handles local interrupts (timer, thermal, performance monitoring) and receives IPIs (inter-processor interrupts). I/O APIC: routes external interrupts to CPUs. Key registers: ICR (interrupt command register, for IPIs), LVT (local vector table, for timer/LINT/thermal/PMI), TPR (task priority register), EOI register.

ext.spec: Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer's Manual
ext.summary: The APIC (Local APIC + I/O APIC) is the modern interrupt controller for x86 multi-core systems. Local APIC: per-CPU, handles local interrupts (timer, thermal, performance monitoring) and receives IPIs (inter-processor interrupts). I/O APIC: routes external interrupts to CPUs. Key registers: ICR (interrupt command register, for IPIs), LVT (local vector table, for timer/LINT/thermal/PMI), TPR (task priority register), EOI register.

structure.meaning: Unique ID for each CPU's local APIC (0-255).

Sends IPIs: vector (8 bits), delivery mode (3 bits: fixed, lowest priority, SMI, NMI, INIT, startup), destination mode (physical/logical), level (assert/deassert), trigger (edge/level), destination shorthand, destination ID.
Local vector table entry for the APIC timer: vector, delivery mode, mask, timer mode (one-shot/periodic/TSC-deadline).
Local vector table for LINT0 and LINT1 (external interrupts from 8259 or I/O APIC).
Task priority (0-15). Interrupts with priority <= TPR are masked.
Write to signal end of interrupt processing.
Redirection Table Entry: vector, delivery mode, destination mode, polarity, trigger, mask, destination.

notes: APIC replaces the 8259 PIC in modern x86 systems.
Local APIC is per-CPU; I/O APIC is shared (routes external interrupts).
IPIs (Inter-Processor Interrupts) enable SMP communication (TLB shootdown, rescheduling).
APIC timer supports one-shot, periodic, and TSC-deadline modes.
x2APIC extends the APIC to support more than 255 CPUs (using MSR access instead of MMIO).
